metadata.title: LearningO - Math / Read
metadata.subject: Math
metadata.generated_for: Children with dyslexia and other learning differences, approx. ages 5-10
design_principles: Every question requires reading printed numerals, equations, symbols, or short problem text - no audio does the work.
Formal mathematical notation (+, -, >, <, =) is introduced and read directly, building the bridge to written maths.
Wrong options are never random. Each one names a specific misconception (miscounting, operation reversal, digit-order confusion).
Three difficulty bands rotate inside every type: easy for fluency, medium for the learning edge, happy for pure joy.
Data handling (pictographs) and logical reasoning are introduced as their own strands, not just folded into word problems.
Feedback praises the process, never the child's intelligence.
Read-aloud support (audio_text) remains available as an accommodation on every item, even though the target skill is print reading.
Safety, honesty and help-seeking items carry a mastery_weight above 1.0 so they surface in reports even when accuracy overall is high.

tts_guidance.note: Read audio_text exactly as written when read-aloud support is used. For sequence and multi-select items, pause 500ms between listed items.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: translating a counted visual set into a written numeral
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: The most basic visual counting task - confirms one-to-one counting and numeral matching together.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: decoding mathematical symbols and computing the result
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: First formal written-equation task, connecting symbol reading directly to calculation.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: checking whether a calculation as written is correct
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Verification is a distinct skill from calculation - useful for catching mistakes in any future working.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: working backward from a known result to find an unknown part
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Early algebraic thinking - the unknown can be in any position, not just at the end.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: matching a comparison symbol to the correct relationship between two numbers
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Formalises number comparison into standard mathematical notation used throughout later schooling.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: identifying a visual rule and predicting the next item
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Visual patterns build the same reasoning as number patterns, using a different, sometimes easier, channel.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: reading a shape's written name and matching it visually
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Print-based shape ID, connecting written vocabulary directly to geometric recognition.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: holding several numeral-to-quantity matches in mind at once
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Multi-item version of counting, testing whether cardinality holds up under a small memory load.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: counting and comparing groups arranged differently
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Tests true number conservation - that count matters more than spread-out arrangement or shape.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: reading a short story, extracting numbers, and calculating
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: The print equivalent of the Listen module's story task - now decoding is also required.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: applying one numeric rule (odd/even, more/less than) repeatedly across a set
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Tests whether an abstract rule, once grasped, can be applied consistently across several numbers.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: translating a numeral into spatial position
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Builds the mental number line that underlies all later estimation, rounding, and comparison work.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: counting symbols in a graph and answering a question about the data
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: First data-handling skill in the bank - reading, not just calculating, is the core demand.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: extracting a value from a visual clock or coin representation
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: Visual (not just spoken) time and money reading, closer to how these skills are used in daily independent life.

question_type_registry.primary_construct: drawing a valid conclusion from given numeric relationships
question_type_registry.diagnostic_purpose: The ceiling task of the module - true reasoning from facts, not just calculation, the skill all later maths builds on.

difficulty_band.easy: Consolidation. Child should succeed ~90% of the time. Builds fluency and confidence.
difficulty_band.medium: Learning edge. Target ~65-75% success. This is where growth data lives.
difficulty_band.happy: Pure joy question. Near-certain success, silly or warm content, low mastery weight. Placed to reset mood after effort and to keep the session feeling like play.

reporting_recipes.skill_profile: Group accuracy by academic.skill and cognition.process to find the child's cognitive shape (e.g. strong discriminate / weak sequence).
reporting_recipes.life_skill_radar: Group accuracy by life_skill.domain across all subjects to build a 14-spoke life-skill radar chart per child.
reporting_recipes.dyslexia_error_map: Count wrong answers by distractor_insight value, not just by question. The distractor tells you WHY, so one wrong tap becomes a diagnosis.
reporting_recipes.attention_curve: Plot time_to_first_touch and accuracy against telemetry.session_position to find the child's real attention span, then cap session length there.
reporting_recipes.working_memory_ceiling: Accuracy vs cognition.working_memory_load. The load level where accuracy drops below 60% is the child's current WM ceiling - never exceed it during teaching.
reporting_recipes.confidence_calibration: Compare the wellbeing.confidence_prompt answer with actual correctness. Confident+wrong = misconception to correct. Unsure+right = needs reassurance, not more teaching.
reporting_recipes.impulsivity_index: Wrong answers where time_to_first_touch < 25% of expected_response_time_ms. High index means teach 'wait and think', not more content.
reporting_recipes.persistence_index: Retry rate and abandon rate on medium-band items. Falling persistence over weeks is an early wellbeing flag.
reporting_recipes.mood_trend: Track emotion_checkin responses over sessions. Two sad check-ins in a row should lower difficulty automatically for the next session.
reporting_recipes.personality_map: Aggregate personality_signal outcomes to describe tendencies (e.g. cautious, highly pro-social, low help-seeking) for the parent report.

wellbeing_rules: No question ever shows a countdown clock. Speed is rewarded, never punished.
Feedback praises the process ('you listened right to the end'), never the child's intelligence.
After two wrong answers the app shows how it works instead of asking again.
A happy-band question follows any run of three errors.
Every safety and help-seeking question points the child towards a trusted grown-up.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Count the pictures. Tap the number.
hints: Count each apple once.
questions.worked_example: Touch each picture once as you count. Stop at the last one.

feedback.correct: 3. Correctly counted. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Touch each apple as you count it.
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: counting a visible set and matching a numeral

life_skill.hidden_lesson: Careful counting means you always know exactly how much you have.

analysis.primary_construct: translating a counted visual set into a written numeral
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: The most basic visual counting task - confirms one-to-one counting and numeral matching together.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Answers that are consistently one more or one less than correct suggest a counting-sequence slip, not a numeral-reading issue.
analysis.parent_note: This is the visual twin of listening-based counting - both matter for full number sense.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Have your child point to each item while counting aloud.

hints: What number, minus 15, leaves 18? Add them back together.
questions.worked_example: What number, added to the others, would make this true?

feedback.correct: 33. Correctly found the missing start, even with bigger numbers. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Add 15 back onto 18 to find the starting number.
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: solving for an unknown in a simple equation

life_skill.primary: Finding a missing amount with bigger numbers
life_skill.hidden_lesson: This working-backward trick is genuinely useful for checking any subtraction.

analysis.primary_construct: working backward from a known result to find an unknown part
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Early algebraic thinking - the unknown can be in any position, not just at the end.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Answering with the total instead of the missing part shows the equation's structure wasn't fully parsed.
analysis.parent_note: This is the very first seed of algebra, long before x and y appear.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Cover the blank with a finger and ask what number would make it balance.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Which symbol makes it true?

distractor_insight.>: calculated one side but skipped comparing to the other
distractor_insight.=: calculated one side but skipped comparing to the other

hints: Work out both sides before comparing.
questions.worked_example: The wide open side of the symbol always faces the bigger number.

feedback.correct: < . 14 is less than 15, both sides worked out and correctly compared. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Work out 7x2 and 6+9 separately, then compare the results.
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: using greater-than, less-than, and equals symbols

life_skill.hidden_lesson: This kind of comparison mixes two different operations in one question.

analysis.primary_construct: matching a comparison symbol to the correct relationship between two numbers
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Formalises number comparison into standard mathematical notation used throughout later schooling.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Consistently reversing > and < shows the symbol's direction, not the comparison itself, is the issue.
analysis.parent_note: These symbols look similar, so a mix-up here is about symbol memory, not maths sense.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Remember: the symbol's open mouth always points to the bigger number.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Look at the pattern. Tap what comes next.

distractor_insight.🔵: repeated the last item instead of continuing the alternation
distractor_insight.🟢: introduced a colour not in the pattern

hints: The colours swap every time.
questions.worked_example: What's the rule? Apply it once more to find what's next.

feedback.correct: 🔴. The alternating pattern continued correctly. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: The pattern swaps colours each time. What comes after blue?
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: extending a visual number or shape pattern

life_skill.hidden_lesson: Patterns are everywhere, from clothing designs to floor tiles.

analysis.primary_construct: identifying a visual rule and predicting the next item
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Visual patterns build the same reasoning as number patterns, using a different, sometimes easier, channel.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Repeating the whole pattern from the start instead of continuing it shows the sequence, not the growth rule, was noticed.
analysis.parent_note: Visual pattern spotting often comes more naturally to some children than the number version.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Build the pattern with real objects and ask what piece comes next before checking.

hints: Two greens, then one yellow, repeating.

academic.skill: extending a visual number or shape pattern

life_skill.hidden_lesson: This same skill helps you spot a mistake in a repeating design.

analysis.primary_construct: identifying a visual rule and predicting the next item
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Visual patterns build the same reasoning as number patterns, using a different, sometimes easier, channel.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Repeating the whole pattern from the start instead of continuing it shows the sequence, not the growth rule, was noticed.

hints: 这些组的数量很接近——仔细数一数。

feedback.correct: 全部三组都匹配正确,即使数量很接近。🔢

ja.instruction: 数字と絵のグループを合わせよう。
ja.prompt: 数字と絵のグループを合わせよう。

feedback.correct: 近い数でも3つとも正しく合わせられたね。🔢
feedback.incorrect: これらのグループは数が近いよ。それぞれしっかり数えよう。
feedback.second_try: 一緒にやってみよう。やり方を見てね。

hints: 이 묶음들은 크기가 비슷해요 - 꼼꼼히 세어 보세요.
ko.worked_example: 한 묶음을 세어 보세요. 그 숫자를 찾으세요. 그다음 묶음으로 넘어가세요.

feedback.correct: 크기가 비슷해도 세 개 모두 정확히 짝지었어요. 🔢

feedback.second_try: 이 문제는 같이 풀어봐요 - 어떻게 푸는지 잘 보세요.

id.instruction: Cocokkan setiap angka dengan kelompok gambarnya.
hints: Kelompok-kelompok ini ukurannya berdekatan - hitung dengan teliti.
id.worked_example: Hitung satu kelompok. Temukan angkanya. Lalu lanjut ke kelompok berikutnya.

feedback.correct: Ketiganya berhasil dicocokkan, meskipun ukurannya berdekatan. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Kelompok-kelompok ini ukurannya berdekatan. Hitung masing-masing sampai selesai.
feedback.second_try: Ayo kita coba bersama - lihat caranya.

vi.instruction: Ghép mỗi số với nhóm hình ảnh của nó.
vi.prompt: Ghép mỗi số với nhóm của nó.
hints: Các nhóm này có số lượng gần nhau - đếm cẩn thận.
vi.worked_example: Đếm một nhóm. Tìm số của nó. Rồi chuyển sang nhóm tiếp theo.

feedback.correct: Cả ba khớp đúng, dù với số lượng gần nhau. 🔢

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Match each number to its group of pictures.
questions.prompt: Match each number to its group.
hints: These groups are close in size - count carefully.
questions.worked_example: Count one group. Find its number. Then move to the next.

feedback.correct: All three matched, even at bigger sizes. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Count each balloon group fully before matching.
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: matching numerals to quantities across several items

life_skill.hidden_lesson: At bigger sizes, counting in twos can help check your total.

analysis.primary_construct: holding several numeral-to-quantity matches in mind at once
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Multi-item version of counting, testing whether cardinality holds up under a small memory load.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Correct on early pairs but wrong later shows fatigue or load, not a counting-concept gap.
analysis.parent_note: This tests counting stamina across several items, not just one at a time.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Cover all but one pair at a time to reduce the load while practising.

es.instruction: Relaciona cada número con su grupo de imágenes.
es.prompt: Relaciona cada número con su grupo.

feedback.correct: Los tres relacionados correctamente, incluso con tamaños más grandes. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Cuenta cada grupo de globos por completo antes de relacionarlo.

fr.instruction: Associe chaque nombre à son groupe d'images.
fr.prompt: Associe chaque nombre à son groupe.

feedback.correct: Les trois bien associés, même avec de plus grandes tailles. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Compte chaque groupe de ballons entièrement avant d'associer.

pt.prompt: Combine cada número com seu grupo.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Tap the two groups with the same amount.

distractor_insight.Left group: assumed the more bunched group has fewer
distractor_insight.Right group: assumed the more spread-out group has more

hints: Count each group - does spacing change the amount?
questions.worked_example: Count each group fully, no matter how it's arranged. Compare the totals.

feedback.correct: Neither - both are equal at 3, no matter how spread out. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Count both groups fully. Spacing doesn't change the count.

academic.skill: recognising equal quantities across different arrangements

life_skill.primary: Understanding that arrangement doesn't change amount
life_skill.hidden_lesson: A spread-out group and a bunched-up group can still be exactly the same size.

analysis.primary_construct: counting and comparing groups arranged differently
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Tests true number conservation - that count matters more than spread-out arrangement or shape.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Picking groups that look similarly spread out, rather than counting each one, shows arrangement is overriding true counting.
analysis.parent_note: A spread-out group of 5 and a bunched-up group of 5 are still both 5 - this checks that understanding directly.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Rearrange a group of objects and recount together to show the amount doesn't change.

questions.note: both groups shown have 3 apples, spaced differently

distractor_insight.Different: assumed different-looking spread means different amount

hints: Count both groups of grapes carefully.
questions.worked_example: Count each group fully, no matter how it's arranged. Compare the totals.

feedback.correct: Same - both are 5, correctly counted. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Count each group fully. Are they really different amounts?
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: recognising equal quantities across different arrangements

life_skill.primary: Understanding that arrangement doesn't change amount
life_skill.hidden_lesson: It's tempting to guess from how spread out a group looks - counting is always more reliable.

analysis.primary_construct: counting and comparing groups arranged differently
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Tests true number conservation - that count matters more than spread-out arrangement or shape.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Picking groups that look similarly spread out, rather than counting each one, shows arrangement is overriding true counting.
analysis.parent_note: A spread-out group of 5 and a bunched-up group of 5 are still both 5 - this checks that understanding directly.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Rearrange a group of objects and recount together to show the amount doesn't change.

es.instruction: Toca los dos grupos con la misma cantidad.
hints: Cuenta con cuidado ambos grupos de uvas.
es.worked_example: Cuenta cada grupo por completo, sin importar cómo esté organizado. Compara los totales.

feedback.correct: Igual: ambos son 5, contados correctamente. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Cuenta cada grupo por completo. ¿Son realmente cantidades diferentes?
feedback.second_try: Hagamos este juntos: mira cómo se hace.

fr.instruction: Touche les deux groupes qui ont la même quantité.
hints: Compte les deux groupes de raisins avec attention.
fr.worked_example: Compte chaque groupe entièrement, peu importe comment il est disposé. Compare les totaux.

feedback.correct: Identique - les deux valent 5, bien comptés. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Compte chaque groupe entièrement. Sont-ils vraiment différents ?
feedback.second_try: Faisons-le ensemble - regarde comment ça marche.

pt.instruction: Toque nos dois grupos com a mesma quantidade.
hints: Conte os dois grupos de uvas com cuidado.
pt.worked_example: Conte cada grupo por completo, não importa como está organizado. Compare os totais.

feedback.correct: Igual - ambos têm 5, contados corretamente. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Conte cada grupo por completo. Eles são realmente quantidades diferentes?
feedback.second_try: Vamos fazer esta juntos - veja como funciona.

it.instruction: Tocca i due gruppi con la stessa quantità.
hints: Conta con attenzione entrambi i gruppi d'uva.
it.worked_example: Conta ogni gruppo per intero, non importa come è disposto. Confronta i totali.

feedback.correct: Uguali - sono entrambi 5, contati correttamente. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Conta ogni gruppo per intero. Sono davvero quantità diverse?
feedback.second_try: Facciamo questo insieme - guarda come si fa.

de.instruction: Tippe auf die zwei Gruppen mit der gleichen Anzahl.
hints: Zähl beide Traubengruppen sorgfältig.
de.worked_example: Zähl jede Gruppe vollständig, egal wie sie angeordnet ist. Vergleiche die Gesamtzahlen.

feedback.correct: Gleich – beide haben 5, richtig gezählt. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Zähl jede Gruppe vollständig. Sind es wirklich unterschiedliche Mengen?
feedback.second_try: Lass uns das gemeinsam machen – schau, wie es funktioniert.

nl.instruction: Tik op de twee groepen met evenveel.
hints: Tel beide groepen druiven zorgvuldig.
nl.worked_example: Tel elke groep helemaal, ongeacht hoe die is gerangschikt. Vergelijk de totalen.

feedback.correct: Gelijk - beide zijn 5, juist geteld. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Tel elke groep helemaal. Zijn het echt verschillende aantallen?
feedback.second_try: Laten we dit samen doen - kijk hoe het werkt.

ru.instruction: Нажми на две группы с одинаковым количеством.
hints: Посчитай обе группы винограда внимательно.
ru.worked_example: Посчитай каждую группу полностью, независимо от того, как она расположена. Сравни итоги.

feedback.correct: Одинаково — в обеих по 5, правильно посчитано. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Посчитай каждую группу полностью. Действительно ли количество разное?
feedback.second_try: Давай сделаем это вместе — смотри, как это работает.

tr.instruction: Miktarı aynı olan iki gruba dokun.
hints: Her iki üzüm grubunu da dikkatlice say.
tr.worked_example: Nasıl dizilmiş olursa olsun her grubu tam olarak say. Toplamları karşılaştır.

feedback.correct: Aynı - ikisi de 5, doğru sayıldı. 🔢
feedback.incorrect: Her grubu tam olarak say. Gerçekten farklı mı?

hints: 仔细数一数两组葡萄。

hints: 포도 두 묶음을 꼼꼼히 세어 보세요.

id.instruction: Sentuh dua kelompok dengan jumlah yang sama.
hints: Hitung kedua kelompok anggur dengan teliti.

vi.instruction: Chạm vào hai nhóm có cùng số lượng.
hints: Đếm cẩn thận cả hai nhóm nho.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Tap the two groups with the same amount.

distractor_insight.Different: assumed different-looking spread means different amount

hints: Count both groups of toys carefully.
questions.worked_example: Count each group fully, no matter how it's arranged. Compare the totals.

feedback.correct: Same - both are 8, correctly counted. 🧸
feedback.incorrect: Count each group of toys fully before deciding.
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: recognising equal quantities across different arrangements

life_skill.primary: Checking your own belongings are all accounted for
life_skill.hidden_lesson: Checking a full set of toys is there, exactly, is real everyday counting practice.

analysis.primary_construct: counting and comparing groups arranged differently
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: Tests true number conservation - that count matters more than spread-out arrangement or shape.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Picking groups that look similarly spread out, rather than counting each one, shows arrangement is overriding true counting.
analysis.parent_note: A spread-out group of 5 and a bunched-up group of 5 are still both 5 - this checks that understanding directly.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Rearrange a group of objects and recount together to show the amount doesn't change.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Read the problem. Tap the answer.
questions.prompt: Tom has 4 apples. His friend gives him 3 more. How many apples does Tom have now?

feedback.incorrect: Start with four, then add three more.

academic.skill: solving a one-step word problem from print

analysis.primary_construct: reading a short story, extracting numbers, and calculating
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: The print equivalent of the Listen module's story task - now decoding is also required.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Using the wrong operation despite correctly decoding the numbers shows the story's action, not the reading, was the gap.
analysis.parent_note: Real maths problems almost always arrive as a sentence, on paper or on a screen - this is that exact skill.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Underline the numbers and circle the action word (gave, took, shared) before solving.

hints: 这条规则说的是正方形,不是所有有四条相等边的形状。
zh.worked_example: 这些信息能确定告诉你什么?排除掉不确定的选项。

feedback.correct: 不一定——这条规则只告诉你正方形具有这个性质,并没有说只有正方形才有。🧠
feedback.incorrect: 原来的规则只是单方向的:正方形有四条相等的边。它没说只有正方形才有。
feedback.second_try: 我们一起来做这一题——看看是怎么做的。

ja.instruction: よく読んで。必ず正しいと言える答えをタップしよう。
ja.prompt: 正方形はみんな4つの辺の長さが同じです。この形は4つの辺の長さが同じです。これは必ず正方形？
options: 必ずしもそうとは言えない - 別の形かもしれない
ja.correct_answer: 必ずしもそうとは言えない - 別の形かもしれない
accepted_answers: 必ずしもそうとは言えない - 別の形かもしれない
hints: このルールは正方形について教えてくれるけど、4つの辺が同じ長さの形すべてについてではないよ。
ja.worked_example: 事実から、確実に言えることは何かな? はっきりしないことは除外しよう。

feedback.correct: 必ずしもそうとは言えない - ルールは正方形にはこの性質があると言っているだけで、この性質を持つのが正方形だけとは言っていないよ。🧠
feedback.incorrect: 元のルールは一方向だけだよ: 正方形は4つの辺が同じ。正方形だけがそうだとは言っていないよ。
feedback.second_try: 一緒にやってみよう。やり方を見てね。

ko.instruction: 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요. 반드시 맞는 답을 누르세요.
ko.prompt: 모든 네모는 네 변의 길이가 같아요. 이 모양은 네 변의 길이가 같아요. 이 모양은 반드시 네모일까요?
options: 꼭 그렇지는 않다 - 다른 모양일 수도 있다
ko.correct_answer: 꼭 그렇지는 않다 - 다른 모양일 수도 있다
accepted_answers: 꼭 그렇지는 않다 - 다른 모양일 수도 있다
hints: 그 규칙은 네모에 대한 것이지, 네 변의 길이가 같은 모든 모양에 대한 것은 아니에요.
ko.worked_example: 이 사실들이 확실히 알려주는 것은 무엇인가요? 확실하지 않은 것은 제외하세요.

feedback.correct: 꼭 그렇지는 않아요 - 규칙은 네모가 이 성질을 가진다고만 했지, 네모만 그렇다고는 하지 않았어요. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: 원래 규칙은 한쪽 방향이에요: 네모는 네 변의 길이가 같아요. 네모만 그렇다고는 하지 않았어요.
feedback.second_try: 이 문제는 같이 풀어봐요 - 어떻게 푸는지 잘 보세요.

id.instruction: Baca dengan teliti. Sentuh jawaban yang pasti benar.
id.prompt: Semua persegi memiliki empat sisi sama panjang. Bentuk ini memiliki empat sisi sama panjang. Haruskah ini persegi?
options: Belum tentu - bisa jadi bentuk lain
id.correct_answer: Belum tentu - bisa jadi bentuk lain
accepted_answers: Belum tentu - bisa jadi bentuk lain
hints: Aturan ini memberitahu tentang persegi, bukan tentang setiap bentuk dengan empat sisi sama panjang.
id.worked_example: Apa yang pasti diberitahukan oleh fakta-fakta ini? Singkirkan apa pun yang tidak pasti.

feedback.correct: Belum tentu - aturan ini hanya memberitahu bahwa persegi memiliki sifat ini, bukan bahwa hanya persegi yang memilikinya. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Aturan aslinya hanya berlaku satu arah: persegi memiliki empat sisi sama panjang. Ini tidak berarti hanya persegi yang memilikinya.
feedback.second_try: Ayo kita coba bersama - lihat caranya.

vi.instruction: Đọc kỹ. Chạm vào câu trả lời chắc chắn đúng.
vi.prompt: Mọi hình vuông đều có bốn cạnh bằng nhau. Hình này có bốn cạnh bằng nhau. Nó có chắc là hình vuông không?
options: Không chắc chắn - nó có thể là một hình khác
vi.correct_answer: Không chắc chắn - nó có thể là một hình khác
accepted_answers: Không chắc chắn - nó có thể là một hình khác
hints: Quy tắc nói về hình vuông, không nói về mọi hình có bốn cạnh bằng nhau.
vi.worked_example: Các thông tin chắc chắn cho bạn biết điều gì? Loại bỏ những điều không chắc chắn.

feedback.correct: Không chắc chắn - quy tắc chỉ cho biết hình vuông có đặc điểm này, không nói rằng chỉ hình vuông mới có. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Quy tắc ban đầu chỉ đi một chiều: hình vuông có bốn cạnh bằng nhau. Nó không nói rằng chỉ hình vuông mới có.
feedback.second_try: Hãy cùng làm câu này - xem cách thực hiện nhé.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Read carefully. Tap the answer that must be true.
questions.prompt: Ben is older than Sam. Sam is older than Mia. Who is the oldest?

distractor_insight.Sam: correctly placed in the middle but not identified as the oldest
distractor_insight.Mia: identified as the youngest instead of the oldest

hints: Follow the chain: Ben > Sam > Mia.
questions.worked_example: What do the facts definitely tell you? Rule out anything that isn't certain.

feedback.correct: Ben. The full chain reasoned correctly. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Follow the chain of ages from oldest to youngest.
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: logical reasoning from stated numeric facts

life_skill.hidden_lesson: Chaining facts together to find an answer is real logical reasoning, not just memory.

analysis.primary_construct: drawing a valid conclusion from given numeric relationships
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: The ceiling task of the module - true reasoning from facts, not just calculation, the skill all later maths builds on.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Strong reasoning here despite slower calculation elsewhere is the classic profile worth protecting and flagging in a report.
analysis.parent_note: If your child reasons well here even when calculation is slow, that gap matters more than raw speed.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Talk through the logic out loud together rather than rushing to an answer.

es.instruction: Lee con atención. Toca la respuesta que debe ser verdadera.

feedback.incorrect: Sigue la cadena de edades de mayor a menor.
feedback.second_try: Hagamos este juntos: mira cómo se hace.

fr.instruction: Lis avec attention. Touche la réponse qui doit être vraie.

feedback.incorrect: Suis la chaîne des âges du plus âgé au plus jeune.

pt.instruction: Leia com cuidado. Toque na resposta que deve ser verdadeira.

ko.instruction: 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요. 반드시 맞는 답을 누르세요.

feedback.second_try: Hãy cùng làm câu này - xem cách thực hiện nhé.

questions.subject: Math

questions.correct_answer: It is not from the box
accepted_answers: It is not from the box

distractor_insight.It is from the box: directly contradicts the observed fact about the key
distractor_insight.The front door is broken: introduces an explanation not supported by the given facts

hints: If every key in the box works, but this one doesn't, where must it be from?
questions.worked_example: What do the facts definitely tell you? Rule out anything that isn't certain.

feedback.correct: It is not from the box - since every key in the box does work. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Every key in the box works. If this one doesn't, can it be from the box?
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

life_skill.hidden_lesson: This kind of reasoning helps you notice when something doesn't fit an expected pattern.

analysis.primary_construct: drawing a valid conclusion from given numeric relationships
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: The ceiling task of the module - true reasoning from facts, not just calculation, the skill all later maths builds on.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Strong reasoning here despite slower calculation elsewhere is the classic profile worth protecting and flagging in a report.
analysis.parent_note: If your child reasons well here even when calculation is slow, that gap matters more than raw speed.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Talk through the logic out loud together rather than rushing to an answer.

es.instruction: Lee con atención. Toca la respuesta que debe ser verdadera.

feedback.incorrect: Todas las llaves de la caja funcionan. Si esta no funciona, ¿puede ser de la caja?
feedback.second_try: Hagamos este juntos: mira cómo se hace.

fr.instruction: Lis avec attention. Touche la réponse qui doit être vraie.

fr.correct_answer: Elle ne vient pas de la boîte
accepted_answers: Elle ne vient pas de la boîte
hints: Si chaque clé de la boîte fonctionne, mais que celle-ci ne fonctionne pas, d'où doit-elle venir ?
fr.worked_example: Qu'est-ce que les faits te disent avec certitude ? Élimine tout ce qui n'est pas certain.

feedback.correct: Elle ne vient pas de la boîte - puisque chaque clé de la boîte fonctionne. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Chaque clé de la boîte fonctionne. Si celle-ci ne fonctionne pas, peut-elle venir de la boîte ?
feedback.second_try: Faisons-le ensemble - regarde comment ça marche.

pt.instruction: Leia com cuidado. Toque na resposta que deve ser verdadeira.
pt.prompt: Toda chave na caixa abre a porta da frente. Você encontra uma chave que NÃO abre a porta da frente. O que deve ser verdadeiro?
options: A porta da frente está quebrada
hints: Se toda chave na caixa funciona, mas esta não, de onde ela deve ser?
pt.worked_example: O que os fatos realmente dizem? Descarte tudo o que não é certo.

feedback.correct: Ela não é da caixa - já que toda chave na caixa funciona. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Toda chave na caixa funciona. Se esta não funciona, ela pode ser da caixa?
feedback.second_try: Vamos fazer esta juntos - veja como funciona.

it.instruction: Leggi con attenzione. Tocca la risposta che deve essere vera.
it.prompt: Ogni chiave nella scatola apre la porta d'ingresso. Trovi una chiave che NON apre la porta d'ingresso. Cosa deve essere vero?
hints: Se ogni chiave nella scatola funziona, ma questa non funziona, da dove deve provenire?

feedback.incorrect: Ogni chiave nella scatola funziona. Se questa non funziona, può provenire dalla scatola?
feedback.second_try: Facciamo questo insieme - guarda come si fa.

feedback.correct: Er ist nicht aus der Box – denn jeder Schlüssel in der Box funktioniert. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Jeder Schlüssel in der Box funktioniert. Wenn dieser nicht funktioniert, kann er aus der Box sein?
feedback.second_try: Lass uns das gemeinsam machen – schau, wie es funktioniert.

zh.instruction: 仔细读一读。点出一定正确的答案。

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Read carefully. Tap the answer that must be true.
questions.prompt: Ana has more coins than Ben. Ben has more coins than Cara. If Cara has 5 coins, what do we know for certain about Ana?

distractor_insight.Ana has exactly 5 coins: ignored the chain and just repeated Cara's amount

hints: Follow the chain: Ana > Ben > Cara, and Cara has 5.
questions.worked_example: What do the facts definitely tell you? Rule out anything that isn't certain.

feedback.correct: Ana has more than 5 coins - since she has more than Ben, who has more than Cara's 5. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Follow the chain from Cara's known amount up to Ana.
feedback.second_try: Let's do this one together - watch how it works.

academic.skill: logical reasoning from stated numeric facts

life_skill.primary: Chaining comparisons with a real number
life_skill.hidden_lesson: Combining a chain of comparisons with one real number is genuine reasoning, not just counting.

analysis.primary_construct: drawing a valid conclusion from given numeric relationships
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: The ceiling task of the module - true reasoning from facts, not just calculation, the skill all later maths builds on.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Strong reasoning here despite slower calculation elsewhere is the classic profile worth protecting and flagging in a report.
analysis.parent_note: If your child reasons well here even when calculation is slow, that gap matters more than raw speed.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Talk through the logic out loud together rather than rushing to an answer.

es.instruction: Lee con atención. Toca la respuesta que debe ser verdadera.

questions.subject: Math
questions.instruction: Read carefully. Tap the answer that must be true.

questions.correct_answer: Leo finished the race, or someone gave him one another way
accepted_answers: Leo finished the race, or someone gave him one another way

distractor_insight.Leo definitely finished the race himself: assumed the rule works in reverse without justification - a common but genuine reasoning trap

hints: The rule tells you finishing leads to a medal. Does having a medal always mean you finished?
questions.worked_example: What do the facts definitely tell you? Rule out anything that isn't certain.

feedback.correct: Careful thinking - having a medal doesn't strictly prove he finished, unless we also know medals are only ever given for finishing. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: The original rule only goes one way. Having a medal doesn't automatically prove the reverse is true.

academic.skill: logical reasoning from stated numeric facts

life_skill.primary: Careful logical reasoning about reversed rules
life_skill.hidden_lesson: This is a genuinely tricky, advanced idea: a rule and its reverse aren't automatically both true.

analysis.primary_construct: drawing a valid conclusion from given numeric relationships
analysis.diagnostic_purpose: The ceiling task of the module - true reasoning from facts, not just calculation, the skill all later maths builds on.
analysis.behaviour_watch: Strong reasoning here despite slower calculation elsewhere is the classic profile worth protecting and flagging in a report.
analysis.parent_note: If your child reasons well here even when calculation is slow, that gap matters more than raw speed.
analysis.teacher_action_if_missed: Talk through the logic out loud together rather than rushing to an answer.

fr.instruction: Lis avec attention. Touche la réponse qui doit être vraie.

pt.prompt: Toda pessoa que termina a corrida ganha uma medalha. Leo tem uma medalha. O que deve ser verdadeiro?
options: Leo terminou a corrida, ou alguém lhe deu uma de outra forma
Leo com certeza terminou a corrida sozinho
pt.correct_answer: Leo terminou a corrida, ou alguém lhe deu uma de outra forma
accepted_answers: Leo terminou a corrida, ou alguém lhe deu uma de outra forma
hints: A regra diz que terminar leva a uma medalha. Ter uma medalha sempre significa que você terminou?
pt.worked_example: O que os fatos realmente dizem? Descarte tudo o que não é certo.

feedback.correct: Pensamento cuidadoso - ter uma medalha não prova estritamente que ele terminou, a menos que também saibamos que medalhas só são dadas por terminar. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: A regra original vale apenas numa direção. Ter uma medalha não prova automaticamente que o inverso é verdadeiro.
feedback.second_try: Vamos fazer esta juntos - veja como funciona.

it.instruction: Leggi con attenzione. Tocca la risposta che deve essere vera.
it.prompt: Ogni persona che finisce la gara riceve una medaglia. Leo ha una medaglia. Cosa deve essere vero?
options: Leo ha finito la gara, oppure qualcuno gliel'ha data in un altro modo
Leo ha di certo finito la gara da solo
Leo di certo non ha corso
it.correct_answer: Leo ha finito la gara, oppure qualcuno gliel'ha data in un altro modo
accepted_answers: Leo ha finito la gara, oppure qualcuno gliel'ha data in un altro modo
hints: La regola ti dice che finire porta a una medaglia. Avere una medaglia significa sempre che hai finito?
it.worked_example: Cosa ti dicono con certezza i fatti? Escludi tutto ciò che non è certo.

feedback.correct: Ragionamento attento - avere una medaglia non dimostra con certezza che abbia finito, a meno che non sappiamo anche che le medaglie vengono date solo per aver finito. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: La regola originale vale in un solo senso. Avere una medaglia non dimostra automaticamente che sia vero anche il contrario.
feedback.second_try: Facciamo questo insieme - guarda come si fa.

de.instruction: Lies sorgfältig. Tippe auf die Antwort, die sicher stimmen muss.
de.prompt: Jede Person, die das Rennen beendet, bekommt eine Medaille. Leo hat eine Medaille. Was muss wahr sein?
options: Leo hat das Rennen beendet, oder jemand hat ihm auf andere Weise eine gegeben
Leo hat das Rennen definitiv selbst beendet
Leo hat definitiv nicht am Rennen teilgenommen
de.correct_answer: Leo hat das Rennen beendet, oder jemand hat ihm auf andere Weise eine gegeben
accepted_answers: Leo hat das Rennen beendet, oder jemand hat ihm auf andere Weise eine gegeben
hints: Die Regel sagt dir, dass das Beenden zu einer Medaille führt. Bedeutet eine Medaille zu haben immer, dass man beendet hat?
de.worked_example: Was sagen dir die Fakten mit Sicherheit? Schließe alles aus, was nicht sicher ist.

feedback.correct: Vorsichtig gedacht – eine Medaille zu haben beweist nicht sicher, dass er das Rennen beendet hat, außer wir wissen auch, dass Medaillen nur für das Beenden vergeben werden. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Die ursprüngliche Regel gilt nur in eine Richtung. Eine Medaille zu haben beweist nicht automatisch das Gegenteil.
feedback.second_try: Lass uns das gemeinsam machen – schau, wie es funktioniert.

nl.instruction: Lees zorgvuldig. Tik op het antwoord dat zeker waar moet zijn.
nl.prompt: Iedereen die de race uitloopt, krijgt een medaille. Leo heeft een medaille. Wat moet waar zijn?
options: Leo liep de race uit, of iemand gaf hem er op een andere manier een
Leo liep zeker zelf de race uit
Leo deed zeker niet mee aan de race
nl.correct_answer: Leo liep de race uit, of iemand gaf hem er op een andere manier een
accepted_answers: Leo liep de race uit, of iemand gaf hem er op een andere manier een
hints: De regel vertelt je dat uitlopen tot een medaille leidt. Betekent een medaille hebben altijd dat je hebt uitgelopen?
nl.worked_example: Wat vertellen de feiten je zeker? Sluit alles uit wat niet zeker is.

feedback.correct: Goed nagedacht - een medaille hebben bewijst niet strikt dat hij heeft uitgelopen, tenzij we ook weten dat medailles alleen voor het uitlopen worden gegeven. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: De oorspronkelijke regel geldt maar één kant op. Een medaille hebben bewijst niet automatisch het omgekeerde.
feedback.second_try: Laten we dit samen doen - kijk hoe het werkt.

ru.instruction: Прочитай внимательно. Нажми на ответ, который обязательно верен.
ru.prompt: Каждый, кто финиширует в забеге, получает медаль. У Лео есть медаль. Что обязательно верно?
options: Лео финишировал в забеге, или кто-то дал ему медаль другим способом
Лео точно финишировал в забеге сам
Лео точно не участвовал в забеге
ru.correct_answer: Лео финишировал в забеге, или кто-то дал ему медаль другим способом
accepted_answers: Лео финишировал в забеге, или кто-то дал ему медаль другим способом
hints: Правило говорит, что финиш ведёт к медали. Значит ли получение медали, что человек обязательно финишировал?
ru.worked_example: Что факты точно говорят тебе? Отбрось всё, что не является точным.

feedback.correct: Внимательное рассуждение — наличие медали не строго доказывает, что он финишировал, если мы не знаем также, что медали даются только за финиш. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Исходное правило работает только в одну сторону. Наличие медали не автоматически доказывает обратное.
feedback.second_try: Давай сделаем это вместе — смотри, как это работает.

tr.instruction: Dikkatlice oku. Kesinlikle doğru olan cevaba dokun.
tr.prompt: Yarışı bitiren her kişi bir madalya alır. Leo'nun bir madalyası var. Ne kesinlikle doğrudur?
options: Leo yarışı bitirdi veya başka bir şekilde madalya aldı
tr.correct_answer: Leo yarışı bitirdi veya başka bir şekilde madalya aldı
accepted_answers: Leo yarışı bitirdi veya başka bir şekilde madalya aldı
hints: Kural bitirmenin madalyaya yol açtığını söyler. Madalyaya sahip olmak her zaman bitirdiğin anlamına mı gelir?
tr.worked_example: Verilenler sana kesin olarak ne söylüyor? Kesin olmayan her şeyi ele.

feedback.correct: Dikkatli düşünme - madalyaların sadece bitirmek için verildiğini bilmediğimiz sürece, madalyaya sahip olmak kesinlikle bitirdiğini kanıtlamaz. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Asıl kural tek yönlüdür. Madalyaya sahip olmak, tersinin doğru olduğunu otomatik olarak kanıtlamaz.
feedback.second_try: Bunu birlikte yapalım - nasıl yapıldığını izle.

zh.instruction: 仔细读一读。点出一定正确的答案。
zh.prompt: 每个完成比赛的人都会获得一枚奖牌。Leo有一枚奖牌。什么一定是对的?
options: Leo完成了比赛,或者有人用别的方式给了他一枚
Leo肯定是自己完成了比赛
zh.correct_answer: Leo完成了比赛,或者有人用别的方式给了他一枚
accepted_answers: Leo完成了比赛,或者有人用别的方式给了他一枚
hints: 规则告诉你完成比赛会得到奖牌。但有奖牌是否就一定意味着完成了比赛?
zh.worked_example: 这些信息能确定告诉你什么?排除掉不确定的选项。

feedback.correct: 仔细推理——除非我们还知道奖牌只会在完成比赛时颁发,否则有奖牌并不能严格证明他完成了比赛。🧠
feedback.incorrect: 原来的规则只是单方向的。有奖牌并不能自动证明反过来也成立。
feedback.second_try: 我们一起来做这一题——看看是怎么做的。

ja.instruction: よく読んで。必ず正しいと言える答えをタップしよう。
ja.prompt: レースを完走した人はみんなメダルをもらいます。レオはメダルを持っています。何が必ず正しい？
options: レオはレースを完走した、または別の方法でメダルをもらった
レオは絶対に自分でレースを完走した
レオは絶対にレースに出ていない
ja.correct_answer: レオはレースを完走した、または別の方法でメダルをもらった
accepted_answers: レオはレースを完走した、または別の方法でメダルをもらった
hints: ルールは完走するとメダルがもらえると教えてくれるよ。でも、メダルを持っていることが、いつも完走したことを意味する？
ja.worked_example: 事実から、確実に言えることは何かな? はっきりしないことは除外しよう。

feedback.correct: 注意深い考え方だね - メダルを持っているからといって、完走したと確実に証明できるわけじゃないよ。メダルが完走でしか手に入らないとわかっていない限りはね。🧠
feedback.incorrect: 元のルールは一方向だけだよ。メダルを持っていることは、逆が必ず正しいことを自動的には証明しないよ。
feedback.second_try: 一緒にやってみよう。やり方を見てね。

ko.instruction: 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요. 반드시 맞는 답을 누르세요.
ko.prompt: 경주를 끝낸 모든 사람은 메달을 받아요. 레오는 메달을 가지고 있어요. 무엇이 반드시 맞을까요?
options: 레오는 경주를 끝냈거나, 다른 방법으로 메달을 받았다
ko.correct_answer: 레오는 경주를 끝냈거나, 다른 방법으로 메달을 받았다
accepted_answers: 레오는 경주를 끝냈거나, 다른 방법으로 메달을 받았다
hints: 규칙은 경주를 끝내면 메달을 받는다고 했어요. 메달이 있다는 것이 항상 경주를 끝냈다는 뜻일까요?
ko.worked_example: 이 사실들이 확실히 알려주는 것은 무엇인가요? 확실하지 않은 것은 제외하세요.

feedback.correct: 신중한 생각이에요 - 메달이 오직 경주를 끝낸 경우에만 주어진다는 걸 알지 못하면, 메달이 있다고 해서 꼭 경주를 끝냈다는 증거는 아니에요. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: 원래 규칙은 한쪽 방향으로만 성립해요. 메달이 있다고 해서 그 반대가 자동으로 맞는 건 아니에요.
feedback.second_try: 이 문제는 같이 풀어봐요 - 어떻게 푸는지 잘 보세요.

id.instruction: Baca dengan teliti. Sentuh jawaban yang pasti benar.
id.prompt: Setiap orang yang menyelesaikan lomba mendapat medali. Leo memiliki medali. Apa yang pasti benar?
options: Leo menyelesaikan lomba, atau seseorang memberinya medali dengan cara lain
id.correct_answer: Leo menyelesaikan lomba, atau seseorang memberinya medali dengan cara lain
accepted_answers: Leo menyelesaikan lomba, atau seseorang memberinya medali dengan cara lain
hints: Aturan ini memberitahu bahwa menyelesaikan lomba menghasilkan medali. Apakah memiliki medali selalu berarti kamu menyelesaikan lomba?
id.worked_example: Apa yang pasti diberitahukan oleh fakta-fakta ini? Singkirkan apa pun yang tidak pasti.

feedback.correct: Pemikiran yang teliti - memiliki medali tidak sepenuhnya membuktikan dia menyelesaikan lomba, kecuali kita juga tahu medali hanya diberikan untuk itu. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Aturan aslinya hanya berlaku satu arah. Memiliki medali tidak secara otomatis membuktikan kebalikannya benar.
feedback.second_try: Ayo kita coba bersama - lihat caranya.

vi.instruction: Đọc kỹ. Chạm vào câu trả lời chắc chắn đúng.
vi.prompt: Mọi người hoàn thành cuộc đua đều nhận được huy chương. Leo có một huy chương. Điều gì chắc chắn đúng?
options: Leo đã hoàn thành cuộc đua, hoặc ai đó đã cho anh ấy huy chương bằng cách khác
Leo chắc chắn đã tự mình hoàn thành cuộc đua
Leo chắc chắn không tham gia cuộc đua
vi.correct_answer: Leo đã hoàn thành cuộc đua, hoặc ai đó đã cho anh ấy huy chương bằng cách khác
accepted_answers: Leo đã hoàn thành cuộc đua, hoặc ai đó đã cho anh ấy huy chương bằng cách khác
hints: Quy tắc cho biết hoàn thành thì có huy chương. Có huy chương luôn có nghĩa là đã hoàn thành không?
vi.worked_example: Các thông tin chắc chắn cho bạn biết điều gì? Loại bỏ những điều không chắc chắn.

feedback.correct: Suy nghĩ cẩn thận - có huy chương không chắc chắn chứng minh anh ấy đã hoàn thành, trừ khi ta cũng biết huy chương chỉ được trao cho người hoàn thành. 🧠
feedback.incorrect: Quy tắc ban đầu chỉ đi một chiều. Có huy chương không tự động chứng minh điều ngược lại là đúng.
feedback.second_try: Hãy cùng làm câu này - xem cách thực hiện nhé.
